 Daniel Radcliffe Wants to Reunite with 'Kill Your Darlings' Co-Star for a New Project
 Parade Follow Alexandria Ingham Add to Preferred Sources Mon, November 9, 2026 at 4:09 PM UTC Daniel Radcliffe Wants to Reunite with 'Kill Your Darlings' Co-Star for a New Project When you think of Daniel Radcliffe , there's no doubt that you think of his breakout role of Harry Potter in the Harry Potter film franchise. However, since getting his start in the 1999 BBC adaptation of David Copperfield , he has gone on to land more than 50 credits to his name.
 His most recent performances have been in The Fall and Rise of Reggie Dinkins , the NBC mockumentary series with Tracy Morgan , and the animated movie Steps for Netflix. It was during the premiere of Steps that he gushed about reuniting with Jonathan Groff on his upcoming thriller, Trust the Man .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement While reuniting with Groff was a dream come true, there are other co-stars he would love to work with again. He did tell People that it's easier to say who he doesn't want to reunite with, but he wasn't there for the negativity, so he didn't go into more details.
 Instead, he focused on the positives, sharing that he would love to work with Dane DeHaan again. He loved his time working with him on Kill Your Darlings , and added, "I would love to do something else with him at some point."
 Kill Your Darlings was a 2013 American biographical drama following the college lives of those who would become known as the Beat Generation's leading members. Radcliffe played Allen Ginsberg, and DeHaan took on the role of Lucien Carr, and together, they told the story of how the two would go on to meet William S. Burroughs ( Ben Foster) and Jack Kerouac ( Jack Huston ) and form the literary movement known as The New Vision. Michael C. Hall, David Cross , and Elizabeth Olsen also starred. 
 However, for now, Radcliffe is focused on promoting his newer movies and TV shows. At the premiere of Steps , where he voices the Prince, he noted that it was great to finally do something his three-year-old son can watch right away.
 Advertisement Advertisement Steps , which is a charming Cinderella -esque story that focuses on the sisters, will stream on Netflix on Nov. 20, 2026.
